answer: Batching attestations into one commit cheapens verification only when that commit is bound to a Merkle root over distinct signer keys. Without the binding, an operator holding N disposable identities lodges a single pulse of bulk countersigns, pays one commit fee, and buries every false attestation under it, so the 70% verification pool flows to one colluding plume of clones at near-zero marginal cost. Charge per leaf and expand signer keys so Sybil cost stays linear: forging N seats costs N seat fees plus a slashed bond, removing the ledge that turns volume into free trust.
